 The Doña Ana County Clerk’s Office sent out an email Monday correcting what it said was inaccurate information about early voting times and hours in a previously mailed election notice.
 Early voting will run from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday and 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Saturdays through Oct. 31 at the Doña Ana County Government Center, 845 N. Motel Boulevard, Las Cruces. It will run from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. Tuesdays through Saturdays, again through Oct. 31, at the following other locations:
 Anthony Library, 750 Landers Road, Anthony
 Corbett Center (New Mexico State University), 1600 International Mall, Las Cruces
 Doña Ana Community College Chaparral, 755 Prescott Anthony Drive, Chaparral
 DACC East Mesa, 2800 Sonoma Ranch Boulevard, Las Cruces
 DACC Sunland Park, 3365 McNutt Road, Sunland Park
 Hatch Valley Public Schools Student Services Center, 350 Main St., Hatch
 Las Cruces City Hall, 700 N. Main St., Las Cruces
 Mesilla Town Hall, 2231 Avenida de Mesilla, Mesilla
 “The Doña Ana County Clerk’s Office apologizes for the error and any confusion or inconvenience it may have caused,” the email states. “The office is committed to providing voters with reliable election information and appreciates the community’s understanding.”
 In related news, an absentee ballot drop-off box at 1000 McNutt Road in Sunland Park is back up and running after being struck by a semitrailer on Oct. 6. Voters can drop off ballots there 24/7 through 7 p.m. on Election Day, Nov. 3.
 New America again
 President Donald Trump on Monday once again suggested renaming New Mexico “New America,” prompting a fresh wave of condemnation from the state’s Democrats.
 “New Mexico should immediately change its name to New America,” Trump wrote in a post on his Truth Social website. “We are not Mexico, we are the United States of America! The name would add great value and prestige to the State! Home Values and Incomes would rise, and you would be even prouder while saluting our beautiful American Flag! Maybe even the Crooked Elections, that New Mexico is known for, would become honest again!”
 Republican candidate for Congress Greg Cunningham, left, debates Democratic U.S. Rep. Gabe Vasquez for New Mexico’s 2nd Congressional District seat in October.
 Image from video 
 Trump first floated the idea in a Truth Social post in early September , not long after he renamed Lake Ontario “Lake America” amid a trade dispute with Canada. He has floated the idea several times since, including in social media posts, in a speech at the Republican midterm convention in Texas and in a video endorsing Republican congressional candidate Greg Cunningham.
 U.S. Rep. Gabe Vasquez, the Democratic incumbent who Cunningham is trying to unseat in New Mexico’s 2nd Congressional District, once again condemned the idea.
 “Greg Cunningham’s boss is doubling down on this ridiculous proposal — shouldn’t the President be spending his time figuring out how to lower prices for Americans?” Vasquez wrote in a social media post. “Of course he’s not. And Greg will stay silent again — he can’t even defend our state’s name.”
 The issue has come up in the contest between the two before, including during a debate last week , where Cunningham said he is “a proud New Mexican” and opposes renaming the state.
 Other Democrats who spoke out anew on Monday included Rep. Melanie Stansbury and Sen. Ben Ray Luján.
 “New Mexico’s name dates back hundreds of years, long before the United States even existed,” Luján said in a statement. “It carries generations of history, culture, and rich traditions that continue to shape who we are.”
 “Mr. President, our state is not yours to rename,” Stansbury wrote on BlueSky . “Our history is not yours to erase. Our culture and identity run deep, shaped by generations of New Mexicans long before you or the U.S. were here at all.”
 New Mexico Republicans have generally said they oppose changing the state’s name while also sometimes dismissing Democratic outrage over Trump’s statements as a distraction.
 “I stand by my original statement — New Mexico does not need a new name,” Republican gubernatorial candidate Gregg Hull said Monday in a statement to Source New Mexico. “Our identity is defined by our rich culture, our beautiful landscape, and the resilience of our people. That identity is never up for negotiation. EVER.”
 “To no surprise, Democrats and their outrage about this non-issue is ANOTHER attempt to distract from their total failure running New Mexico’s state government,” state Senate Republicans said in a Facebook post . “It’s simple: New Mexico needs New Leadership!”
 Nathan Brown is the assistant city editor of The New Mexican .
